prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1449; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's alright.

Q: That's fine. For the record, can you describe where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on the main road in Baytown, heading toward the shopping center. It was a normal weekday afternoon, traffic was moderate.

Q: What were you doing just before the impact?

A: I was in my lane, going maybe thirty miles an hour. The other car came over from the opposite side. I hit the brakes but there wasn't time to get out of the way.

Q: Would you say this was a head-on impact, or was there some angle to it?

A: It was pretty much straight on, front to front. Both of our front ends hit. It didn't feel like a huge crash, but it was enough to push me back in the seat.

Q: Did your airbags deploy?

A: No, they didn't. I think it was just below the threshold for that.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: How are you feeling physically since the collision?

A: My neck is really stiff and sore. Turning my head to check traffic hurts. I've also got a headache that comes and goes, and my shoulders ache by the end of the day.

Q: Have you sought medical attention?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same evening. They told me it looked like whiplash and gave me a neck brace and some pain medication.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the collision or your injuries?

A: Just that I'm still having trouble sleeping because of the neck pain. I'd like to get this resolved as soon as possible.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
